external_entities.name: podcaster
external_entities.description: A person who publishes a show: uploads each episode's audio.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Podcasters publish their shows with us.

external_entities.name: podcast app
external_entities.description: A listener's podcast app, which polls each show's RSS feed all day and downloads episodes. The source does not say where an app downloads an episode from, so the model holds no flow for it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Listeners' podcast apps fetch each show's RSS feed from the feed service, which is public.

external_entities.name: ad partner
external_entities.description: The ad partner, which sends files of download counts every night.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Every night our ad partner sends us files of download counts.

processes.name: upload API
processes.description: Takes each episode's audio file from podcasters over the internet, refuses an upload that would take a show over its 50 GB of storage, and stores the audio in the media store and the episode details in the show database.
processes.source_excerpt: A podcaster uploads each episode's audio file through the upload API, which is on the internet.
processes.notes: Stated quota: "Each show gets 50 GB of storage in total, and the upload API refuses an upload that would take a show over its 50 GB." A size limit on one file is hedged, not stated: "Leo says the upload API probably also has a size limit on a single file, but he would have to check."

processes.name: transcoder
processes.description: Picks up each new audio file from the media store and makes the smaller versions that listeners' apps download. Each transcoder runs at most two jobs at once.
processes.source_excerpt: The transcoder picks up each new audio file from the media store and makes the smaller versions that listeners' apps download.
processes.notes: Stated concurrency limit: "Each transcoder runs at most two jobs at once." The source does not say where the smaller versions are kept.

processes.name: feed service
processes.description: The public service that builds each show's RSS feed from the show database and serves it to podcast apps. It has no rate limit.
processes.source_excerpt: Listeners' podcast apps fetch each show's RSS feed from the feed service, which is public.
processes.notes: Stated absence of a rate limit: "We do not rate limit the feed service, because apps poll feeds all day and we never want an app to miss a new episode."

processes.name: stats importer
processes.description: Starts a new import job for every file of download counts the ad partner sends, with no cap on how many run together, and writes the counts to the stats database.
processes.source_excerpt: The stats importer starts a new import job for every file that arrives, with no cap on how many run together, and writes the counts to the stats database.
processes.notes: Stated absence of a concurrency limit: "with no cap on how many run together".

data_stores.name: media store
data_stores.description: Holds each episode's uploaded audio file.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The upload API stores the audio in the media store and the episode details in the show database.

data_stores.name: show database
data_stores.description: Holds the episode details of every show, which the feed service reads to build each feed.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The upload API stores the audio in the media store and the episode details in the show database.

data_stores.name: stats database
data_stores.description: Holds the download counts the stats importer writes.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The stats importer starts a new import job for every file that arrives, with no cap on how many run together, and writes the counts to the stats database.

data_flows.name: upload episodes
data_flows.description: A podcaster signs in and uploads an episode's audio file and its details.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A podcaster uploads each episode's audio file through the upload API, which is on the internet.
data_flows.authentication: password sign-in with an email address
data_flows.data_description: episode audio files and episode details
data_flows.notes: "Podcasters sign in with an email address and a password."

data_flows.name: store audio
data_flows.description: The upload API stores each episode's audio in the media store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The upload API stores the audio in the media store and the episode details in the show database.

data_flows.name: store episode details
data_flows.description: The upload API stores each episode's details in the show database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The upload API stores the audio in the media store and the episode details in the show database.

data_flows.name: pick up audio
data_flows.description: The transcoder picks up each new audio file from the media store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The transcoder picks up each new audio file from the media store and makes the smaller versions that listeners' apps download.

data_flows.name: fetch feeds
data_flows.description: A podcast app fetches a show's RSS feed, and polls it all day.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Listeners' podcast apps fetch each show's RSS feed from the feed service, which is public.

data_flows.name: read show details
data_flows.description: The feed service reads the show database to build each feed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The feed service reads the show database to build each feed.

data_flows.name: send download counts
data_flows.description: The ad partner sends files of download counts every night.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night our ad partner sends us files of download counts.

data_flows.name: write counts
data_flows.description: Each import job writes the download counts to the stats database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The stats importer starts a new import job for every file that arrives, with no cap on how many run together, and writes the counts to the stats database.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Where podcasters, podcast apps and the ad partner reach the hosting account from.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A podcaster uploads each episode's audio file through the upload API, which is on the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: hosting account
trust_boundaries.description: The one hosting account everything the platform team runs is in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: All of this runs in one hosting account. The podcasters, the listeners' apps and the ad partner are outside it.

assumptions.assumption: The feed service presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It serves each show's RSS feed to podcast apps that fetch it, and an RSS feed is a document fetched by its URL, the HTTP family that prompts/extract.md calls web.

assumptions.assumption: Podcasters are placed on the internet because the schema requires a zone.
assumptions.basis: They reach the upload API on the internet; the source places them outside the hosting account and says no more.

assumptions.assumption: Podcast apps are placed on the internet because the schema requires a zone.
assumptions.basis: They fetch feeds from the public feed service; the source places them outside the hosting account and says no more.

assumptions.assumption: The ad partner is placed on the internet because the schema requires a zone.
assumptions.basis: The source places it outside the hosting account and does not say how its files arrive.
